x: Indra, the most powerful Rigvedic god, was called Purandara, the destroyer of forts. Varuna upheld Rita, Agni was the fire god and Soma the god of the sacred drink.
t: Recall the epithet of each Rigvedic deity.

x: The Rigveda contains hymns, the Yajurveda sacrificial formulas and procedures, the Samaveda verses chanted at ceremonies and the Atharvaveda spells and charms, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall the content of each Veda.

x: Both are true and R explains A: Varuna is linked with Rita because Rita is the cosmic and natural order that he guards, which is why he is called Ritasyagopa.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: I and II are correct: the six orthodox systems are Sankhya, Yoga, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Mimamsa and Vedanta. III is false because Lokayata is a heterodox materialist school and Kapalika a Shaiva sect.
t: Recall the six orthodox darshanas.

x: Purva Mimamsa deals with Karmakanda, the ritual portion of the Vedas, and Uttara Mimamsa (Vedanta) deals with Jnanakanda, the knowledge portion. Option C reverses the pair.
t: Watch the order of the pair.

x: Option B is incorrect: Buddha was born at Lumbini; Kushinagar is the place of his Mahaparinirvana. The first sermon at Sarnath and enlightenment at Bodh Gaya are right.
t: Match each place with the event in Buddha's life.

x: Lumbini was Buddha's birthplace, Sarnath saw the first sermon, women were admitted as Bhikshunis at Vaishali, and Anathapindika donated the Jetavana Vihara, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.
t: Recall the event linked with each place.

x: Both are true and R explains A: the Tripitaka is a collection because it comprises three baskets, the Vinaya (monastic rules), Sutta (discourses) and Abhidhamma (philosophy).
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: The Sarvastivada school held that dharmas exist in the past, present and future. The Ajivikas were a separate sect, Vajrayana is tantric Buddhism and the Chishtis are a Sufi order.
t: Recall the doctrine of each Buddhist school.

x: Rishabhdev was the first Tirthankara, Parshvanath the 23rd, Mahavira the 24th and last, and Mahaprajapati the first woman to enter the Buddhist Sangha, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.
t: Recall the place of each Tirthankara.

x: I, II and III are correct: Mahavira attained Kaivalya at Jrimbhik village on the Rijupalika, and Nirvana at Pavapuri in 527 BCE; Parshvanath attained Nirvana at Sammed Shikhar.
t: Check each place and date separately.

x: Heliodorus, a Greek envoy, erected the Garuda Pillar at Besnagar and called himself a Bhagavata. The Khalsa is Sikh, Pubharama Buddhist and the Barabar Caves Ajivika.
t: Link the person to the monument.

x: Shankaracharya taught Advaitavada, Ramanuja Vishishtadvaita, Tulsidas wrote the Ramcharitmanas in Awadhi and Raskhan wrote Prem Vatika, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Recall the work or doctrine of each saint.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Bakhtiyar Kaki being his disciple does not account for Muinuddin Chishti settling at Ajmer and founding the Chishti order in India.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Guru Nanak founded Sikhism with Ik Onkar, Guru Arjan Dev was the fifth Guru who compiled the Adi Granth, Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa in 1699 and Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed in Delhi in 1675, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
t: Recall the role of each Guru.

x: Brahmo Sabha came in 1828, Tattvabodhini Sabha in 1839, Arya Samaj in 1875 and Ramakrishna Mission in 1897, giving A, B, C, D.
t: Arrange the movements by year.

x: All four are correct: Akbar abolished the pilgrimage tax and jizya, built the Ibadat Khana in 1575 and introduced Din-i-Ilahi (Tauhid-i-Ilahi) in 1582.
t: Check each date and policy.

x: Agni has about 200 hymns, Soma has the whole ninth Mandala, Aghanya means a cow not to be killed, and the Boghaz-Koi inscription names Indra, Varuna, Mitra and Nasatya, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall the fact linked with each term.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Brahman as ultimate reality and Atman as the self are two separate Upanishadic concepts, and one does not define the other.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: In Mimamsa, Apurva is the unseen force that links a ritual act (karma) with its later result. Ultimate reality is Brahman, liberation is Moksha and the self is Atman.
t: Discriminate Mimamsa terms from Upanishadic ones.

x: Patanjali's eightfold Yoga runs Yama, Niyama, Asana, Pranayama, Pratyahara, Dharana, Dhyana and Samadhi, so Samadhi is the final limb.
t: Recall the order of the eight limbs.

x: Both are true: the Four Noble Truths concern suffering, its cause, its cessation and the path, and the Dharmachakrapravartana Sutta is Buddha's first sermon at Sarnath.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: A Chaitya is a prayer hall, a Vihara a monks' residence, a Stupa a relic or burial mound and the Vinaya Pitaka the monastic rules, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Recall the function of each term.

x: The Digha Nikaya holds the long Suttas, the Mahavamsa is a Sri Lankan Buddhist chronicle, the Sutta Pitaka holds Buddha's discourses and the Abhidhamma Pitaka gives the philosophy, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Recall the content of each text.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: the Guhyasamaja matters for its tantric teaching, not because Vajrayana flourished from the eighth century.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Samvara is the stoppage of the inflow of karma. Elimination of existing karma is Nirjara, relativity of knowledge is Syadvada and gradual fasting is Sallekhana.
t: Discriminate Samvara from Nirjara.

x: Triratna means Right Faith, Right Knowledge and Right Conduct, Syadvada is relativity of knowledge, Sallekhana is the last vow of fasting and Digambara means sky-clad, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall the meaning of each Jain term.

x: The First Jain Council met at Pataliputra under Sthulabhadra, where the twelve Angas were compiled. The Second met at Vallabhi.
t: Discriminate the venues of the two Jain councils.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Dehatmavada, the identity of body and self, is one doctrine within Charvaka thought, not the cause of its materialism and reliance on perception.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Pashupata was founded by Lakulisha, Kapalikas worshipped Bhairava with skull symbols and ashes, Lingayats followed Basava and the Nathpanth was led by Matsyendranath and Gorakhnath, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
t: Recall the founder or feature of each Shaiva sect.

x: The Alvars were Vishnu devotees, the Nayanars Shiva devotees, Chaitanya a Krishna devotee of Bengal and Kabir the author of Sakhi, Sabad and Ramaini, giving a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
t: Discriminate Alvars from Nayanars.

x: The Suhrawardis followed Bahauddin Zakariya in Multan and Sindh, the Firdausis Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri in Bihar, the Naqshbandis Ahmad Sirhindi, and the Qadiris Abdul Qadir Jilani, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall the saint and region of each Sufi order.

x: Both are true: the Ramakrishna Mission was non-political, non-sectarian and humanitarian, and Vivekananda joined pure Vedanta with belief in the truth of all religions.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Early Vedic religion centred on worship of nature gods through yajnas and was polytheistic. Image worship and temples came much later.
t: Discriminate early Vedic practice from later developments.

x: Both are true: in the Upanishads, Karma is action and its consequence, and Moksha is liberation from the cycle of rebirth.
t: Check each concept separately.

x: Kapila is the earliest teacher of Sankhya, whose Satkaryavada holds that the effect already exists in its cause. Patanjali is linked with Yoga, Lakulisha with Pashupata and Makkhali Gosala with the Ajivikas.
t: Match each school with its founder.

x: Anathapindika donated the Jetavana Vihara, Vishakha built Pubharama, Bimbisara gave Venuvana and the Sangha was the monastic order, giving a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.
t: Recall the gift linked with each patron.

x: All four are Ajivika: Makkhali Gosala led the sect, Niyativada (fate) was its doctrine, Ashoka and Dasharatha were patrons, and the Barabar and Nagarjuni caves were given to its monks.
t: Check each item against the Ajivika sect.

x: The Second Jain Council met at Vallabhi under Devardhigani Kshamashraman, where the canon was written down. The First met at Pataliputra.
t: Discriminate the venues of the two Jain councils.

x: Ahimsa is non-violence, Satya truth, Brahmacharya chastity and Aparigraha non-possession, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall the meaning of each Mahavrata.

x: The Gupta kings called themselves Parambhagavata and used the Garuda emblem, marking them as Vaishnavas. Advaita, khanqahs and Sama belong to other traditions.
t: Link the dynasty with its religious titles.

x: Both are true: a khanqah was a Sufi hospice where saints lived, and Sama was a musical and spiritual gathering.
t: Check each Sufi term separately.

x: Akbar built the Ibadat Khana in 1575 and opened it to followers of all religions in 1578. The Mahzar came in 1579 and Din-i-Ilahi in 1582.
t: Arrange Akbar's religious steps by year.

x: Akbar issued the Mahzarnama in 1579, claiming final authority on religious disputes. The Ibadat Khana came in 1575 and Din-i-Ilahi in 1582.
t: Recall the year of each religious measure of Akbar.

x: The Brahmo Samaj opposed idol worship, Sati and child marriage. The other options describe Vedic, Jain and Sufi features.
t: Link the reform body to the evils it fought.

x: Both are true and R explains A: Ramakrishna saw Hari, Ram, Allah and Christ as names of one God because he taught the unity behind all religions.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: The Bhakti movement began in South India, in the Tamil country, with the Alvars and Nayanars. Multan, Punjab-Sindh and Bihar are linked with Sufi orders.
t: Recall where Bhakti began.

x: The Rigveda is the oldest Veda, the Yajurveda holds sacrificial formulas, the Samaveda is for ritual chanting, and the Boghaz-Koi inscription of Asia Minor (c. 1400 BC) names Indra, Mitra, Varuna and the Nasatyas, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Recall each Veda's content, then place the foreign inscription.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Rigveda
(b) Yajurveda
(c) Samaveda
(d) Boghaz-Koi Inscription

List-II
(i) Asia Minor record naming Indra, Mitra, Varuna and the Nasatyas
(ii) Ritual chanting
(iii) Oldest Veda
(iv) Sacrificial formulas and procedures

x: I and II are correct: Buddha was born at Lumbini and attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya. III is false because the first sermon was at Sarnath; Kushinagar is where he died.
t: Match each place with the event in Buddha's life.

x: Mahavira was born at Kundagram near Vaishali. He attained Nirvana at Pavapuri; Vallabhi hosted a Jain council and Sammed Shikhar is linked with Parshvanath.
t: Discriminate the birthplace from other Jain sites.

x: Jain sacred literature is called the Agam (Agamas). The Digha Nikaya and Mahavamsa are Buddhist, and the Adi Granth is Sikh.
t: Link each text to its religion.

x: Mattamayura appears in Chedi inscriptions, the Goddess Mahatmya is part of the Markandeya Purana, Ardhanarishvara is the union of Shiva and Shakti, and Vasudeva was called Devadeva, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall the fact linked with each term.

x: Vaishnavism grew out of the older Bhagavata religion of Vasudeva-Krishna, attested by Heliodorus's Garuda Pillar. Pashupata is Shaiva, and the Ajivika and Sufi traditions are unrelated.
t: Link Vasudeva-Krishna worship to its earliest named sect.
s: Vaishnavism developed largely out of which earlier religious tradition centred on the worship of Vasudeva-Krishna?

x: Tulsidas wrote the Ramcharitmanas in Awadhi, Kabir composed Sakhi, Sabad and Ramaini, Chaitanya was the Krishna devotee of Bengal, and Mirabai was the Rajput princess of Mewar devoted to Krishna, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Separate the two Krishna devotees by region and background.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Tulsidas
(b) Kabir
(c) Chaitanya Mahaprabhu
(d) Mirabai

List-II
(i) Rajput princess devoted to Krishna
(ii) Ramcharitmanas in Awadhi
(iii) Sakhi, Sabad and Ramaini
(iv) Krishna devotee associated with Bengal

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Sufism being an ascetic mystical tradition does not explain why Auliya means saints or friends of God.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Kundal is not one of the Five Ks. They are Kesh, Kangha, Kachha, Kara (Kada) and Kripan.
t: Recall the Five Ks.

x: Both are true: Vivekananda spoke at the Parliament of Religions in Chicago in 1893 and founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897.
t: Check each date separately.

x: Jina means conqueror or victor, one who has conquered the senses, which gives Jainism its name. Relativity of knowledge is Syadvada and stoppage of karmic inflow is Samvara.
t: Recall the meaning of the root word.

x: Bakhtiyar Kaki was a disciple of Muinuddin Chishti, Baba Farid taught Nizamuddin Auliya, Nizamuddin was called Mehboob-i-Ilahi and Sultan-ul-Mashaikh, and the Naqshbandis opposed Sama, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall the role of each Sufi figure.

x: Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj at Bombay (Mumbai) in 1875. Ajmer is where he died, not where the Samaj began.
t: Recall where the Arya Samaj was founded.

x: Both are true: Birbal was the leading Hindu to accept Din-i-Ilahi, and Din-i-Ilahi drew on several religious traditions.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Shwetambara means white-clad, the Jain sect whose monks wear white. Digambara means sky-clad, while Kapalika and Pashupata are Shaiva sects.
t: Discriminate the two Jain sects.

x: In Patanjali's Yoga, Yama is the first limb, Niyama the second, Asana the third and Pranayama the fourth, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall the order of the eight limbs.

x: I and II are correct: Parshvanath taught four restraints, and Asteya (non-stealing) is a Mahavrata. III is false because non-possession is Aparigraha, and IV is false because Parshvanath was the 23rd Tirthankara.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: The Nathpanth revered Shiva as Adinath, the first Nath. Bhairava is linked with the Kapalikas, Lakulisha with the Pashupatas and Basava with the Lingayats.
t: Recall the deity of each Shaiva sect.

x: Both are true: Shaktism is a Hindu tradition centred on worship of the Goddess Shakti.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Both are true: Bhakti meant loving devotion to God, and Raskhan was a Muslim poet devoted to Krishna.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: I, II, III and IV are correct: the Adi Granth includes the compositions of Kabir, Baba Farid, Namdev and Raidas along with those of the Sikh Gurus.
t: Check each saint against the Adi Granth.

x: Both are true: Akbar's religious policy rested on tolerance and accommodation of all faiths, seen in the Ibadat Khana debates and Sulh-i-Kul.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Both are true: the Brahmo Sabha of 1828 was a modern reform movement, and Vivekananda is linked with Neo-Hinduism, or Neo-Vedanta.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Aurangzeb reimposed jizya in 1679, reversing Akbar's abolition. 1582 is Din-i-Ilahi, 1579 the Mahzar and 1675 the execution of Guru Tegh Bahadur.
t: Recall the year of each event.

x: Advaita was taught by Adi Shankaracharya, Vishishtadvaita by Ramanujacharya, Dvaita by Madhvacharya, and Lokayata is the Charvaka school, giving a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i.
t: Recall the teacher of each school.

x: I, II, III and IV are correct: Buddhism and Jainism are Nastika schools, the Ajivikas taught Niyativada (fate), and Pashupata Shaivism was founded by Lakulisha.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Shunyavada, the doctrine of emptiness of the Madhyamaka school, was taught by Nagarjuna. Shankara taught Advaita, Ramanuja Vishishtadvaita and Madhva Dvaita.
t: Discriminate Buddhist doctrines from Vedanta schools.
